subject: Simulate data with standardized = TRUE not entirely standardized?

messages.author: 84e6ff87e445f88b
messages.subject: Simulate data with standardized = TRUE not entirely standardized?
parts:
Hello,
I have started to use simulateData() which is fantastic! I have a question though. The standardized = True seems to standardized most variables except for Y in the following model and I don't know why. As a consequence the covariance and correlation matrices are not equal and the estimates are not equal to std.all estimates. Maybe it's not meant to be?

library(lavaan)
population.model <-
'
            Y ~ 0.40*X +0.30*C + 0.50*U
            X ~ 0.30*C + 0.50*U
            '

myData <- simulateData(population.model, model.type="sem",sample.nobs=1000000,return.type="data.frame",standardized=T)
(cov1=cov(myData)) #variances are standardized except for Y, not sure why
(cor1=cor(myData)) 
# cov and cor matrices not equal as Y not standardized

#fit the underlying model on simulated data, including U
modelfit <-'
            Y ~ X +C + U
            X ~ C + U
                    '
fit <- sem( modelfit, data=myData,estimator="GLS")
parameterEstimates(fit,standardized=T)
#est and std.all are not equal as variance of Y is not standardized

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Simulate data with standardized = TRUE not entirely standardized?
parts:
True. It is better to use the simstandard package for this. See also

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/46

Yves.
